reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend, getNextDate and RSchedule/recurConfigToRSchedule helpers and adds shared predicates (isDailyWeekendSkip, isWeekendOrHoliday) in shared/schedules.

duplication.why: The occurrence pipeline (drop daily weekend/holiday days, then shift with getDateWithSkippedWeekend) is written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and schedule-template keeps two copies of its own skipWeekend ternary, now also threading holidays.

placement.why: Core rules sit in shared/schedules, but the range search-window heuristic getMaxWeekendShiftDays lives in server/schedules/app.ts beside a sibling heuristic getDailySearchLimit in shared, and the date pipelines live in handlers rather than one shared function.

scope.why: Changes stay within schedule date logic, its consumers and tests; the parseRecurDate data addition is needed for the new rules.

maintainability.why: Helpers are well named, but four call paths each assemble the skip/drop/shift sequence and two different take/window heuristics must be kept consistent, and schedule-template's inverted noSkipWeekend argument is hard to read.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and schedule-template.ts re-assemble the filter-and-shift logic instead of going through getNextDate or a single shared occurrence function.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange repeats getUpcomingDates' occurrences -> filter -> getDateWithSkippedWeekend -> dayFromDate chain with different bounds and a dedupe step, and getNextDate expresses the same filter as a .find.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-drop branch with its own take window; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template each re-implement the daily-drop/shift handling.
